ca_castle_rock_north_side.blurb: This is the north-facing side of the big, oblong Castle Rock formation in Joshua Tree National Park, beside Belle Campground at roughly 3,800 feet. Nearly all of its 18 climbs are traditional, with one toprope. The grades start at very easy and run up through 5.12, with a notable cluster around 5.11 and a thin scattering of moderates in between. Expect a steeper, smoother wall than the neighbouring south side, with a blend of crack and face lines. The wall stays shaded for most of the day, which suits warm afternoons. The walk from the campground is only about a minute, and the north side holds more routes than the south.

ca_cattle_pocket_the.blurb: The Cattle Pocket is a wall of rock towers in the northern Alabama Hills outside Lone Pine, in the Eastern Sierra at about 4,700 feet. Its 18 climbs are mostly bolted sport, with a handful of trad lines and two ropes-down toprope problems. Grades are weighted toward the middle: a good number of 5.8s and a solid group of 5.10s, with a few easier routes at the bottom and one 5.13 at the top. The rock here is typical Alabama Hills high-desert stone, and the base sits just above the road, so walking in is short and several turnouts are close by.

_expect.name: East Face of the Elephant Head (The Caves)

ca_east_face_of_the_elephant_head_the_ca.blurb: The Caves is the tall, steep east face of Elephant Head, the first big formation you meet on the way into Texas Canyon in the Angeles National Forest, north of Santa Clarita. Big hollows run along the foot of the wall. All 18 routes are bolted sport lines, running from 5.10 up to 5.13, with the bulk in the 5.10s to low 5.12s. Climbing is on pockets, knobs and protruding cobbles in conglomerate, which is brittle and breaks easily when wet, so skip it after rain. A 60 m rope is handy on most formations in the canyon.

ca_area_13_left_side.blurb: Area 13 sits in Clark Canyon above Mammoth Lakes at close to 8,000 feet, and the left side is the busiest section of this moderate-friendly cliff. It is the first wall you see walking up the canyon path. Of its 18 routes, 16 are bolted sport and two are trad, running from the mid 5.6 range to about 5.11, with most falling between 5.7 and 5.10. That makes it a good fit for climbers building up on moderates. The final stretch is a hike up a pumice slope to the base. Afternoon thunderstorms can roll in during summer.

ca_mt_whitney.blurb: Mt. Whitney, at 14,505 feet, is the highest summit in the lower 48 and the centrepiece of the High Sierra above Lone Pine. This page covers 18 climbs, mostly alpine routes plus several trad lines and one mountaineering route. Terrain spans third and fourth class scrambles through moderate fifth class, with a good number at 5.10 and 5.11 and a single route at the extreme end. The classic East Face is a long moderate line of roughly thirteen pitches. Approaches go from Whitney Portal up the North Fork, with most parties camping at Iceberg Lake. Expect altitude, afternoon storms and a shaded east face by midday.

ca_fast_food_wall.blurb: Fast Food Wall is a sport wall on the Benches side of the Emeralds, a climbing area near the South Yuba River off Bowman Lake Road north of Lake Tahoe. It holds 18 routes, mostly bolted sport plus a few mixed lines and a single toprope. The grades lean hard: mostly 5.10 and 5.11, a couple of 5.12s and only one easier route near 5.8. The wall catches the afternoon sun, with shade creeping in earlier as the season advances, and unlike the nearby gorge it sits well clear of flood risk. Routes carry fast-food names that make them easy to remember.
ca_fast_food_wall.approach: Follow the dirt road upstream for about 750 yards, then take the cairned trail on the right and pass a metal bench. Keep going where the path steepens; the wall is the last one on the right before the trail swings left over a rocky hill toward the gorge.
